body.limit: At this recommendation fa is limited by the added a-c link lac's 100Mbps capacity and packet/header overhead: lac_util=0.999996 and payload goodput is about 96.4Mbps in E1/E4; lc.queue.length no longer limits fa because fa uses lac and lc carries only fb with zero drops.
body.explanation: Baseline fa shares the saturated lc bottleneck with 80Mbps fb, leaving only about 17.9Mbps (E0). Adding a one-hop a-c link makes fa's shortest path use lac, removing it from lc contention; fa rises to about 96.4Mbps and fb_loss_frac becomes 0.0 (E1,C1,V1). On lac, Cubic, BBR and NewReno all reach the same link-limited payload rate within tolerance (C2,V2), but BBR has zero lac_drops and zero fa_retrans, so it is the robust choice. The remaining limit is lac's 100Mbps rate and MTU/header overhead, not lc queue length or TCP type.

claims.text: Baseline fa_goodput is limited by sharing lc with fb, not by la or lb.
Adding a direct a-c link raises fa_goodput from 17.86Mbps to 96.38Mbps while keeping fb_loss_frac=0.0.
On the direct link, TCP type does not materially change fa_goodput; Cubic, BBR and NewReno are within 0.03% (within tolerance).
BBR is preferred because it has zero lac_drops and zero fa_retrans at the same goodput.
The recommended network is limited by lac's 100Mbps capacity and packet overhead, with lac_util=0.999996.
The small direct-link drop differences are consistent with Cubic/NewReno having much larger maximum fa_inflight than BBR (185344 vs 60816 bytes).
